page:
Performance optimization guide for Vite: slow server starts, slow page loads, slow builds.
- Browser setup: extensions interfere with requests and slow startup/reload
- Incognito mode faster than regular profile
- Dev-only profile without extensions recommended
- Disable cache in browser dev tools while working with Vite server
- Pre-bundled dependencies: hard caching, fast 304 responses
- Community plugin performance varies, out of Vite's control
- Large dependencies in plugins: dynamically import for faster startup
- buildStart, config, configResolved hooks: don't run long operations (awaited during startup)
- resolveId, load, transform hooks: check keyword/extension before full transformation
- vite --debug plugin-transform or vite-plugin-inspect for measuring transform duration
- Async operations give inaccurate timings, treat as rough estimate
- vite --profile: visit site, press p+enter to record .cpuprofile, use speedscope.app
- resolve.extensions default: ['.mjs', '.js', '.mts', '.ts', '.jsx', '.tsx', '.json']
- Explicit import paths faster than implicit resolution (6 filesystem checks example)
- Narrow resolve.extensions list but ensure node_modules compatibility
- this.resolve() hook: only call when needed
- TypeScript: enable moduleResolution: 'bundler' and allowImportingTsExtensions: true
- Barrel files: re-export pattern causes loading all files, import individual APIs instead
- server.warmup option: pre-transform frequently used files
- vite --debug transform: inspect transform durations
- File watchers: watch for frequently used files
- --open or server.open: auto warmup entry point
- CSS vs Sass/Less/Stylus: use CSS for performance
- SVG: import as strings/URLs instead of framework components
- LightningCSS experimental support

sections.manifest:
Review browser setup for performance.
- Browser extensions: interfere with requests, slow startup and reload
- Create dev-only profile without extensions
- Incognito mode faster than regular profile
- Dev tools cache disable: big impact on startup and full-page reload
- Hard caching of pre-bundled dependencies
- Fast 304 responses for source code
How do browser extensions affect Vite performance?

Audit configured Vite plugins for performance issues.
- Internal and official plugins optimized for least work
- Code transformations: regex in dev, full parse in build
- Community plugin performance varies
- Large dependencies: dynamically import to reduce Node.js startup
- vite-plugin-react#212, vite-plugin-pwa#244 examples
- buildStart, config, configResolved hooks: avoid long operations (awaited during startup)
- resolveId, load, transform hooks: check id/code before full transformation
- Request waterfall: longer transform = more waterfall
- vite --debug plugin-transform: measure transform duration
- vite-plugin-inspect: inspect intermediate plugin state
- Async operations: inaccurate timings, treat as rough estimate
- vite --profile: record .cpuprofile, use speedscope.app for inspection
How do plugin hooks affect performance?

Reduce resolve operations for performance.
- resolve.extensions default: ['.mjs', '.js', '.mts', '.ts', '.jsx', '.tsx', '.json']
- Import './Component.jsx' as './Component': 6 filesystem checks needed
- Explicit import paths faster than implicit
- Narrow resolve.extensions but ensure node_modules compatibility
- this.resolve() in plugins: only call when needed
- TypeScript: moduleResolution: 'bundler' and allowImportingTsExtensions: true
How do resolve operations impact performance?

Avoid barrel files for better performance.
- Barrel files re-export APIs from same directory
- import { slash } from './utils': loads all files even for single API
- All files fetched and transformed due to side-effects
- Load more files than required on initial page load
- Solution: import individual APIs directly (e.g., './utils/slash.js')
- GitHub issue #8237
Why are barrel files bad for performance?

Warm up frequently used files for better performance.
- Dev server on-demand transformation: quick startup, only transform used files
- Import graph only known after file transformation: waterfalls possible
- Example: main.js → BigComponent.vue → big-utils.js → large-data.json
- server.warmup option: pre-transform frequently used files
- vite --debug transform: inspect logs to find frequently transformed files
- Metrics example: /@vite/client 28.72ms, BigComponent.vue 62.95ms, big-utils.js 102.54ms
- Only warm up frequently used files to avoid overload
- --open or server.open: auto warmup entry point
How do I warm up frequently used files?

Use lesser or native tooling for performance.
- Keeping Vite fast: reduce work on source files (JS/TS/CSS)
- CSS instead of Sass/Less/Stylus (nesting via PostCSS/Lightning CSS)
- SVG: import as strings/URLs instead of framework components (React, Vue, etc.)
- Native tooling: LightningCSS experimental support
